# Comwit Template

A Next.js project template with agent instructions, setup skills and custom lint
rules for folder structure and key dependency boundaries.

Source: https://github.com/comwit/template (templates/base in comwit/comwit).
The base source includes Comwit Cloud configuration and the brrrd build adapter.
The root create-comwit pack step exports this pinned source; no separate generic
snapshot is maintained. This migration does not publish a new npm version.

## Start

npm create comwit@latest my-app
cd my-app
pnpm run dev

Optional: --opennext adds Cloudflare Workers configuration and preview/deploy commands.

## Structure

- src/app/: Next.js routes and layouts.
- src/services/{service}/page/{route}/: UI that reads state and calls actions.
- src/services/{service}/state/{domain}/: models, queries and actions.
- src/services/{service}/api/{domain}/: server functions and screen data.
- src/server/repository/: data access, initially backed by in-memory rows in _data/.
- src/lib/: shared UI, state providers and server-function transport.

Default services: app and admin. Dependency direction: page → state → api → repository.
Implement from repository to page. API domains contain index.ts, types.ts and actions/;
state domains also contain model.ts. API actions use createAction and are exposed
through resolveActions. Server Components may fetch initial data for hydration.

## Comwit service setup

The base source is designed for Comwit Cloud. @brrrd/adapter produces dist/brrrd
from next build; scripts/brrrd-adapter.mjs also prepares runtime page manifests.
The preregistered .agents/scripts/comwit-mcp.mjs forwards agent requests to
https://comwit.io/mcp with project context and the local Cloud credential.

Builds, validation and mocked Storybook previews work without real credentials.
For live services, use the Comwit project's setup prompt to prepare the CLI and
.env. COMWIT_PROJECT_ID (MCP) and COMWIT_PROJECT (Cloud) are different IDs.
Run comwit login, then comwit auth export-token --env-out .env; verify with
node .agents/scripts/comwit-mcp.mjs --check. Never print or commit the token.
Use MCP setup_database/setup_storage only for needed resources and follow the
returned nextSteps. Do not invent IDs or register a second MCP server.
Local deployment requires COMWIT_EXECUTION_ENV=local and COMWIT_APP; hosted
sessions use their on-screen Deploy button. Follow the source README and AGENTS.md.

## Instructions and skills

Read AGENTS.md first, then the relevant layer guide:
- src/services/.ai.md: service and import rules.
- src/services/api.ai.md, state.ai.md, page.ai.md: layer conventions.
- src/app/.ai.md: routing and layouts.
- src/server/repository/.ai.md: data models and access.
- src/services/admin/.ai.md: admin routes and accounts.
- .storybook/stories/design-system/design.mdx: UI and style tokens.
- .storybook/stories/.ai.md: page stories and API mocks.

CLAUDE.md references AGENTS.md. Skills live in .agents/skills/;
.claude/skills/ references the same source.
- app-setup: bottom tabs, detail screens, page transitions and PWA install UI.
- auth-setup: per-service Better Auth and Drizzle tables after a database is connected.
- seo-optimize: metadata, JSON-LD, sitemap and robots.
- refactoring: mock-to-database migration when explicitly requested.
- video-offload: move site videos out of the app package.

## Validation

Custom rules in eslint-rules/ are enabled by .oxlintrc.json and executed by Oxlint.
Checks include domain files and exports, route placement, cross-layer deep imports,
direct API access from client pages, direct Drizzle imports in APIs and action wrappers.
Other conventions are documented in the instruction files.

- pnpm run validate: TypeScript and lint.
- pnpm agents:test: skill reference consistency and agent-related regression tests.
- pnpm storybook: real pages and state with APIs mocked in .storybook/mocks/api/.
- pnpm validate:storybook: separate Storybook types, lint and API mock boundary checks.
- pnpm run build: service worker and Next.js build.
- pnpm ui add <name>: install a UI component as source.

## Migrate an existing project

For an existing Next.js App Router project:
1. Scaffold a reference outside the project with create-comwit --no-install --no-git.
2. Inventory routes, data access, authentication and deployment. Keep existing
   infrastructure and behavior unless the requested migration changes them.
3. Copy the applicable instruction files, skills, lint rules and configuration,
   shared code, UI components and Storybook setup. Adapt paths, scripts and
   dependencies to the actual project; do not overwrite existing configuration blindly.
4. Move one domain at a time through repository → api → state → page. Preserve
   authentication and hydration behavior, and update callers before removing old files.
5. Add page stories with mocked APIs. Run validate, agents:test, validate:storybook,
   build-storybook and the production build using the project's package manager.
6. Remove the temporary reference and record adopted conventions and remaining work
   in AGENTS.md.
